The image displays a mango leaf with dark, superficial fungal growth covering a significant portion of its surface. The underlying leaf still appears to be green. This presentation aligns with the description of Sooty Mould, which is characterized by dark, superficial fungal deposits on leaves that grow on insect-secreted honeydew, without infecting the plant tissue itself. The other descriptions do not match; it is not Anthracnose as there are no distinct black spots expanding into dead areas. It is not Die_Back as there is no evidence of twig dieback or leaf scorch. There is no mention of Powdery Mildew in the knowledge base, but the appearance is not consistent with a white, powdery fungus.
